verses.text: At that moment, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “So who’s the greatest in Heaven’s Kingdom?”
Jesus called a little child over and had the child stand right in the middle of them.
He said, “I’m telling you the truth: unless you turn around and become like little children, you won’t enter Heaven’s Kingdom.”
“Whoever humbles themselves like this child is the greatest in Heaven’s Kingdom.”
“Whoever welcomes one child like this in my name welcomes me.”
“But if anyone trips up one of these little ones who believe in me, it’d be better for them to have a huge millstone tied around their neck and be sunk in the deep sea.”
“How terrible for the world, because of all the traps that cause people to stumble! Those traps are bound to come, but how terrible for the person who brings one.”
“If your hand or foot trips you up, cut it off and throw it away. Better to enter life injured or unable to walk than to keep both hands and feet and be thrown into eternal fire.”
“If your eye trips you up, tear it out and throw it away. Better to enter life with one eye than to keep both and be thrown into fiery Gehenna.”
“Don’t look down on even one of these little ones. I’m telling you, their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father in heaven.”
“The Son of Man came to save the lost.”
“What do you think? If someone has a hundred sheep and one wanders off, won’t they leave the ninety-nine and go into the hills looking for the one that’s lost?”
“I’m telling you the truth: if they find it, they’re happier about that one than the ninety-nine that never wandered off.”
“In the same way, your Father in heaven doesn’t want even one of these little ones to be lost.”
“If your brother or sister sins against you, go talk to them one-on-one and show them what went wrong. If they listen, you’ve won your sibling back.”
“If they won’t listen, bring one or two others with you, so the matter can be confirmed by two or three witnesses.”
“If they still won’t listen, bring it to the assembly. If they won’t listen even to the assembly, treat them like a Gentile or a tax collector.”
“I’m telling you the truth: whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven; whatever you release on earth will have been released in heaven.”
“I’m telling you again: if two of you agree on earth about anything you ask for, my Father in heaven will do it for you.”
“Where two or three gather in my name, I’m right there among them.”
Then Peter came up and asked Jesus, “Lord, how many times should I forgive my brother when he sins against me? Seven times?”
Jesus told him, “I’m not saying seven times, but seventy times seven.”
“That’s why Heaven’s Kingdom is like a king who decided to settle accounts with his servants.”
“When he started settling up, they brought him a servant who owed ten thousand talents.”
“The servant couldn’t pay, so his master ordered him, his wife, his children, and everything he owned to be sold to repay the debt.”
“The servant dropped to his knees and begged, ‘Please be patient with me. I’ll pay you back everything!’”
“His master felt compassion, released him, and wiped out the debt.”
“But that same servant went out and found a fellow servant who owed him a hundred denarii. He grabbed him by the throat: ‘Pay me what you owe!’”
“His fellow servant dropped to his knees and begged, ‘Please be patient with me. I’ll pay you back!’”
“But he refused. He went and threw the man in prison until he paid the debt.”
“When the other servants saw what happened, they were deeply upset. They went and told their master everything.”
“Then the master called that servant in: ‘You wicked servant! I wiped out your whole debt because you begged me.”
“‘Shouldn’t you have shown your fellow servant mercy, just as I showed you mercy?’”
“His master was furious and handed him over to the torturers until he paid everything he owed.”
“That’s how my heavenly Father will treat each of you if you don’t forgive your brother or sister from your heart.”
